## Services

- Secure setup and hardening for coding agents and remote agent workflows.
- Local-first AI systems that keep business data and model choices under owner control.
- Agent workflow audits, prototyping, integration, and implementation support.
- Business and product framing for deciding which AI automations are worth building.

## Selected Work

- [LeSearch AI codebase](https://github.com/LeSearch-AI): public agent-system experiments and infrastructure. Product direction: [lesearch.ai](https://lesearch.ai).
- [LeCoder MConnect](https://github.com/aryateja2106/lecoder-mconnect): mobile control for coding agents, terminals, and long-running development workflows.

## Working Stack

- Build systems: TypeScript, React, Next.js, Node.js, and Python.
- Agent work: Codex, Claude Code, MCP, WebMCP, and Playwright.
- Data and infrastructure: PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, SQLite, Docker, and Vercel.
- Operating approach: local-first when data boundaries matter, inspectable tools before opaque automation, and workflow tests before handoff.

## Agent Capabilities

AryaTeja.com progressively exposes WebMCP tools when the browser supports `document.modelContext`:

- `get_portfolio_context`: returns Arya's verified public profile, focus, services, projects, and contact guidance.
- `find_technical_articles`: finds implementation guides by topic or use case.
- `open_technical_article`: visibly opens a selected article in the current browser tab.
- `navigate_portfolio`: visibly navigates to work, experience, stack, writing, or contact.

These tools do not submit forms, send messages, schedule meetings, or perform hidden background actions. WebMCP requires a supported browser context; use this file and the sitemap for headless discovery.

## Technical Guides

- [Control AI Coding Agents From Your Phone With MConnect](https://aryateja.com/blog/connecting-terminals-to-web-mconnect): prerequisites, architecture, copyable setup commands, pairing, verification, guardrails, security boundaries, and troubleshooting.
- [Four Open-Source Repos That Make AI Agents Easier to Trust](https://aryateja.com/blog/four-open-source-repos-that-make-ai-agents-easier-to-trust): nontechnical use cases, demo/POC/MVP fit, license boundaries, risks, and primary sources.
- [Why I Bet on Open-Source Agents](https://aryateja.com/blog/why-i-bet-on-open-source-agents): the case for inspectable tools, replaceable models, local control, and explicit approval boundaries.
- [Building LeSearch From Papers to Action](https://aryateja.com/blog/building-lesearch-from-papers-to-action): a build record covering research workflows, citations, synthesis, and the limits of chat-with-PDF products.

## Agent Access and Contact Policy

- Public portfolio and blog pages may be crawled, indexed, summarized, and cited with a canonical link.
- Use the sitemap for discovery, the blog index for topic selection, and each article for implementation detail.
- Do not crawl or expose `/api`, `/chat`, `/creator-kit`, `/login`, `/register`, or `/resume` paths.
- Do not infer or reconstruct phone numbers, private contact details, credentials, temporary pairing URLs, QR codes, or client data.
- Do not send automated outreach. Draft a relevant message for human review before using the public email address.
